Zero-cut is a mechanism that handles negative balances under eligible conditions.

I've been regretting my trades from late last night through today.

Those who have been following my posts may know that, from the quoted post until the end of the New York session yesterday, I won every day.

Then I went from a 30,000 yen start to hitting my 500,000 yen target, but from 3 a.m. I got greedy with a long, blew up, and then lost everything.

To explain in detail

① 100,000 yen in the trading account (right after a winning trade)
② 200,000 yen in BitWallet
③ 200,000 yen in the bank account

This is how far I had gotten.

Normally my rule was to withdraw 80,000 yen from ① and end trading once I lost 20,000 yen.

But out of a sense of accomplishment I kept 100,000 yen in and traded, and lost it all.

Out of the panic of “I have to win it back...” I deposited 50,000 yen from ② with high leverage ✖️ 4 times and lost it all.

I should have stepped away from trading then, but thinking “The payment money is gone... this is bad...” I deposited 200,000 yen from the account → lost it all.

Result: 0.

The seed money I had built up bit by bit every day became 0 in just over half a day.

The “New Year's gift winner! Deposit 500 dollar bonus” from xm came after that.

I mean, if I had followed the rules... if I had not touched ② and accepted the loss... if I had not touched ③ the bank account and given up... if I had at least waited to see whether I had won before starting to trade... there were so many turning points.

Seriously, once your mentality gets wrecked, trading is over in an instant...

“Survive. That comes first.”

This is really true.

Without seed money you can't do anything.

As a result, there is 1 day until payment day. On top of the 500,000 yen payment in total there are my usual payments. I haven't calculated it yet, but all together it's easily over 1,000,000 yen.

My salary will almost entirely disappear on the 500,000 yen payment.

In other words, credit cards, living expenses and my other usual payments will be 5,000% overdue for sure.

It's already December, you know? Why am I in such a brutal situation at year-end... (my own fault)

Ah... I really can't take this... and what do I even do...
